title: The Verdict of Little Hawley
premise: Emrys Vane, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a private habit of solving the cases the police abandon, is hired by the sister of Maren Little, a girl who vanished from the village of Hawley five years ago and was declared dead after her boyfriend was acquitted. When Emrys receives Maren's diary and finds entries written after her disappearance, they return to Hawley, where the diary's coded references point to a living Maren hiding under a new identity and a village complicit in her flight. Emrys must untangle who helped her vanish, why she staged her own death, and whether exposing her serves justice or destroys the fragile life she built, ending with Emrys choosing to close the case in the only verdict that matters: the truth told to one person, the law kept blind.
about_author: Astrid Ravensworth spent a decade as a court reporter in small-market towns before trading the courtroom for the night desk, a vantage point she claims is the best seat in the house for watching what people do when they think no one is listening. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who keep extraordinary secrets.

chapters.title: The Last Fare Logged
chapters.summary: Emrys Vane, working the graveyard shift at Calloway Cabs, closes their hundredth cold case as a hobbyist and takes a call from a desperate woman named Odette Little. Odette has mailed them her missing sister Maren's diary. Emrys's POV establishes their meticulous, guarded voice and the thrill of an unsolvable case. Beat: restless curiosity tipping into obsession.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Examining the diary, Emrys discovers entries dated weeks after Maren Little's official disappearance five years ago, written in her unmistakable hand. The police declared her dead; her boyfriend, Daniel Croft, was tried and acquitted of her murder. Emrys's POV; the beat is vertigo, a certainty upended, and the decision to take the case no one believes exists.

chapters.title: Arrival at Little Hawley
chapters.summary: Emrys travels to the insular village of Little Hawley, posing as an insurance investigator, and finds a community that flinches at Maren's name. Odette, exhausted and ostracized, gives them Maren's old bedroom. Emrys's POV; the emotional beat is the chill of being watched by an entire village that wants the past buried.

chapters.title: The Acquitted Man
chapters.summary: Emrys tracks down Daniel Croft, now a carpenter living quietly at the village edge, and finds not a killer but a man hollowed out by suspicion. He claims Maren told him, days before she vanished, that she was afraid of someone in her own family. Emrys's POV; beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Coded in the Margins
chapters.summary: Back in Maren's room, Emrys deciphers the diary's marginal symbols as references to village landmarks and dates, including the old quarry and the church restoration fund ledger. Someone helped Maren disappear, and the diary is a map of that conspiracy. Emrys's POV; beat: exhilaration shadowed by the realization that whoever helped her may still be protecting her.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys interviews Reverend Ainsley, keeper of the restoration fund, whose answers are smooth and rehearsed. A ledger page for the year of the disappearance has been razored out. The vicar warns Emrys that some mercies are better left uninvestigated. Emrys's POV; beat: first direct threat, delivered with a smile.

chapters.title: Odette's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Odette, drunk and grieving, nearly admits she knows more than she's said, then retreats, begging Emrys to stop before someone else is hurt. Emrys realizes Odette may have hired them not to find Maren but to confirm she's alive and safe. Emrys's POV; beat: the case tilts from mystery to moral maze.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Gave Back
chapters.summary: Searching the quarry referenced in the diary, Emrys finds a rusted lockbox containing Maren's real identification, a bus ticket, and a photograph of a woman who is not Maren. Someone else vanished that same week and was never reported. Emrys's POV; beat: dread, the discovery that the disappearance had two victims.

chapters.title: The Unreported Woman
chapters.summary: Emrys identifies the photograph's subject as Lena Marsh, a farmhand who left Hawley abruptly in the same season. Her elderly mother remembers Maren and Lena were close, and that Maren came to her once with a bruised face, saying a powerful man in the village hurt her. Emrys's POV; beat: the case reframes from flight to escape.

chapters.title: The Man Everyone Defers To
chapters.summary: Emrys probes Aldous Pemberton, the wealthy landowner whose family funded the church restoration and employs half of Hawley. He is charming, generous, and precise about alibis he was never asked to give. Emrys's POV; beat: cold recognition of a predator protected by gratitude.

chapters.title: A Warning in the Night
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Maren's room and takes the diary while Emrys sleeps, leaving a taxi firm's business card from a rival company as a calling card. Emrys, furious, realizes their investigation has been tracked from the start, possibly through Odette. Emrys's POV; beat: violation and resolve.

chapters.title: The Rival Dispatcher
chapters.summary: Emrys traces the business card to a Hawley cab driver, Silas, who confesses he drove Maren to a coastal bus depot the night she vanished, paid by Pemberton's lawyer to keep quiet. He kept one receipt. Emrys's POV; beat: the first hard evidence, and the terror of what it will cost.

chapters.title: Trial by Memory
chapters.summary: Emrys reconstructs Daniel's trial through old transcripts and press coverage, finding that the prosecution's timeline collapsed because Maren's body was never found, and that one witness recanted overnight. The recanting witness was Silas. Emrys's POV; beat: grief for Daniel, five years wrongly suspected, and anger at a justice system that needed a body to believe a girl.

chapters.title: Odette Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted, Odette admits she helped Maren plan the disappearance after Maren showed her evidence of Pemberton's abuse, but she never knew where Maren went. She hired Emrys because she found a fresh postcard, postmarked this year. Maren is alive, and someone is in contact with her. Emrys's POV; beat: hope and betrayal entangled.

chapters.title: The Postcard Route
chapters.summary: Emrys traces the postcard's postmarks through three forwarding addresses to a seaside town where a woman answering Maren's description works in a bookshop under the name Lena Marsh. Emrys watches her from across the street: alive, wary, unrecognizable by design. Emrys's POV; beat: awe and the weight of the choice now at hand.

chapters.title: The Verdict Before the Trial
chapters.summary: Maren confronts Emrys, revealing she staged her death because no one, not the police, not the village, would believe her against Pemberton, and Daniel's trial was the price of her escape. She begs Emrys to let the verdict stand. Emrys's POV; beat: the collision of two definitions of justice.

chapters.title: Pemberton's Move
chapters.summary: Pemberton's lawyer offers Emrys money to leave, then threatens them with fabricated charges, revealing Pemberton knows Maren lives and has quietly hunted her for years. Emrys realizes the diary was stolen not to hide the past but to find her. Emrys's POV; beat: fear transmuted into urgency, the clock now running.

chapters.title: Closing the Net
chapters.summary: Emrys gathers Silas's receipt, the razored ledger page recovered from the church archive, and Lena Marsh's mother's testimony into a case file aimed at Pemberton rather than Maren, and sends copies to a journalist and a cold-case detective. Emrys's POV; beat: the dispatcher's craft turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Climax
chapters.summary: Pemberton comes for Maren at the bookshop; Emrys, having anticipated the route, has alerted police and stands between them. Pemberton's arrest, aided by Silas's testimony reopened, cracks the village open. Maren must choose in the moment whether to reveal herself. Maren's POV for the first time; beat: terror, then the liberation of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Law Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Pemberton is charged; Maren, as a living witness, testifies under her real name, exonerating Daniel at last, but negotiates immunity for her own false death. The village must live with what its silence cost. Emrys's POV; beat: justice achieved, imperfect and expensive.

chapters.title: The Fare Not Taken
chapters.summary: Daniel, freed from suspicion, asks Emrys why they didn't simply turn Maren in. Emrys reflects that the law wanted a corpse and the truth wanted a witness; only one of them got what it needed. Emrys declines payment from Odette, who begins rebuilding her relationship with her sister. Emrys's POV; beat: quiet satisfaction, the case closed the right way.

chapters.title: The Next Call
chapters.summary: Back on the night shift, Emrys logs one last entry in their private casebook and files the Little Hawley file under 'Closed, Justly.' A new call crackles through the dispatch radio, a voice asking for help with a case everyone else has given up on. Emrys's POV; beat: the cycle renewed, wiser and more wary.
